newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan denies submarine deal kickbacks - papers.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan denies submarine deal kickbacks - papers.

text.p: The Pakistan Navy has denied allegations of kickbacks in a $950 million submarine deal with France, newspapers said on Thursday.
Senior navy officers told Pakistani journalists on Wednesday that there had been no wrongdoing in the deal for three submarines.

The briefing followed allegations in newspapers that kickbacks were received in the 1995 deal that former Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto's government signed with France, some reports targeting Chief of Naval Staff Admiral Mansurul Haque.

"The naval officers made it clear that while the former government may have been involved in corrupt practices, the Agosta deal which it signed was transparent in every sense and was carried out on merit," The News reported.
It quoted an unnamed senior naval officer as saying Haque would volunteer himself for a court martial "if any proof of the charges against him is found".
Islamabad signed an agreement with France in September 1995 to buy three Agosta 90-B submarines.
The government said at the time it had chosen the French vessels after 2-1/2 years of negotiations with French, British, Chinese and Swedish suppliers.
President Farooq Leghari sacked Bhutto's three-year-old government in November on charges of corruption and misrule. Bhutto denies the charges.
Newspapers quoted the navy officers as saying that some former officers were involved in what they called a campaign to malign the armed forces.

The submarine agreement calls for the first vessel to be wholly built in France and delivered within four years. The second would be assembled from parts and completed in Pakistan. The third would be completely built in Karachi.
The Agosta submarines, built in the northwestern French port of Cherbourg, carry torpedoes and SM39 anti-ship missiles.
